report.source_text: During the perioperative period, a 7-day regimen of antiviral treatment (oral valacyclovir 1 g twice a day) and antibiotic therapy (intravenous cefathiamidine 2 g twice a day for 3 days and oral cefuroxime 0.25 g twice a day for 4 days successively) were administered. Granulation tissue formation was observed on the surface of the alveolar wound three weeks after debridement (Fig. 1d). At a follow-up 9 months later, no further tooth exfoliation was found.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Alveolar osteonecrosis following facial herpes zoster
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old man with a 5-week history of right facial erythema, clustered blisters, and severe pain consistent with herpes zoster (HZ) presented with spontaneous exfoliation of four maxillary teeth (teeth 11-17). Physical examination revealed healing HZ scars on the right half of the face and exposed alveolar bone in the right maxilla. Imaging demonstrated decreased bone density, poor socket healing, and empty tooth sockets in the right maxilla. Histopathological examination of the alveolar bone revealed nonvital lamellar bone devoid of osteoblasts and osteocytes, with fibrinoid necrosis of vascular walls and lumen occlusion consistent with ischemic osteonecrosis secondary to HZ vasculitis. Microbiological cultures grew oral commensals (Prevotella denticola, Streptococcus intermedius, Actinomyces species) indicating secondary bacterial colonization rather than primary osteomyelitis. Surgical debridement confirmed extensive malodorous osteonecrosis. The patient was treated with surgical debridement, antiviral therapy (valacyclovir), and antibiotics (cefathiamidine, cefuroxime), with successful outcome demonstrated by granulation tissue formation at 3 weeks and no further tooth exfoliation at 9-month follow-up. The absence of bisphosphonate use or radiation history excluded medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw and osteoradionecrosis.
